subject: MAP: Acme Health — cost stress test & evaluation checklist
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sam Drake <sam@medtech.ai>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 12 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: MAP: Acme Health — cost stress test & evaluation checklist

Hi Sam / Acme procurement,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, we put together a short mutual action plan focused on the evaluation and close timeline with explicit unit-economics checks so your finance and platform teams can validate production cost assumptions. Attaching a lightweight MAP (PDF) plus a sensitivity spreadsheet.

Quick summary of the things we want to lock down during the evaluation:
- Token economics baseline: strings in the MAP are our hosted estimate (gpt-compatible) — baseline = $0.0019 per generated 1k tokens for the selected model variant.
- Typical prompt/response sizes: we assumed 120 tokens in prompt, 450 tokens generated per user interaction (avg). Please confirm if your workflows skew shorter/longer.
- Batching & latency: default continuous-batching yields 2–3x throughput improvements; we need target p95 latency SLOs for the demo flows (we used 250ms).
- Prefix & KV caching: the evaluation will exercise the templated prompts (reusable prefixes). We expect prefix cache hit rate to materially reduce generated tokens — we modeled 18–35% savings depending on reuse patterns.
- Gating rules: if observed tokens/$ > 25% above baseline or tail latency exceeds p95 target, we will (a) enable larger batching windows, (b) recommend quantized model variant, or (c) fallback to smaller context model.

Requested from Acme for the eval plan: sample traffic shape (3-day trace or synthetic), 25 representative prompts, and acceptance criteria for throughput/latency/cost.

Next steps / timeline (proposed):
1) This week: Acme provides sample traffic + 25 prompts (owner: Acme).
2) Week 1–2: Pilot + cost stress test (owner: Redwood - Laura / Rishi).
3) Week 3–4: Full eval with A/B on quantization + caching knobs (owner: Redwood / Acme).
4) Week 5–6: Procurement & contract finalization.

Can we lock a 60-minute walkthrough on Monday to align the traffic shape and acceptance criteria?

Attachments: acme_map_v2.pdf (MAP with milestones), token-econ-sensitivity.xlsx (worksheet: baseline vs stress scenarios)

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Sam Drake <sam@medtech.ai>
To: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2027 09:45:00 -0400
Subject: Re: MAP: Acme Health — cost stress test & evaluation checklist

Laura —

Appreciate the clear MAP. A few clarifying questions from our infra/finance side after a quick pass through the PDF and spreadsheet:

1) Baseline tokens — our average prompt sizes are actually closer to 300 tokens (longer patient context) and generated outputs average ~600 tokens for summarization+instructions. That will increase per-call cost materially. Did you model for variable prompt sizes?

2) Caching assumptions — can you walk us through what counts as a cacheable prefix? For our use case, we have a 3-4 sentence static header + variable patient data. Are there quick wins here?

3) Batching_win vs latency — you mention continuous batching 2–3x throughput: what batching window did you use for the p95 = 250ms estimate? We need the trade-off table to present to our SREs.

4) Quantized models — curious what quality delta you expect for int8-like quantized variants on our summarization prompts. Do you have prior evals we can reference?

If possible, can you put the trade-off numbers into the spreadsheet (latency vs cost vs quality)? We can then run a quick cost projection and follow up with procurement.

Best,
Sam
Director, Platform Engineering
MedTech.AI (Acme Health POC)

Team —

Forwarding Sam's note from Acme. They have longer prompts / outputs than our baseline and asked for concrete numbers on the batching window and cache classification. Rishi — can you run the following and drop the results into the shared sensitivity workbook by EOD tomorrow?

Requests (owner suggested):
- Rishi: run 3 stress scenarios in the sandbox with their approximate sizes (prompt 300 / gen 600):
  a) no caching, batching window 4ms (low-latency)
  b) caching enabled (prefix hit 25%), batching window 8ms
  c) caching enabled, batching window 25ms (higher throughput)
  For each: report p50/p95 latency, tokens generated per minute, and $/1M tokens cost estimate (use our hosted baseline kernel mix). Put results into token-econ-sensitivity.xlsx.
- Karthik: add a short column in the workbook with expected quality delta (%) for int8 vs float16 for summarization prompts (based on prior HelixMed evals). Include recommended fallback thresholds (e.g., quality drop > 3% -> keep float16).
- Vanessa: update the MAP milestones section with explicit acceptance gating language: numeric thresholds for cost (<=25% above baseline), latency (p95 <= 350ms for long prompts), and rollout steps.

We should avoid prematurely recommending model switching until we have the stress numbers. If Rishi's runs show >20% extra cost, propose two mitigations: turn on larger batching and enable prefix caching; if still >20% then present model variant A (quantized) and a rollback plan.

I'm copying the drive link to the workbook here: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1A2B3Cacme-map — please update the spreadsheet tabs: 'scenarios', 'quality-delta', 'rollout-gates'.

Thanks — can we have a short internal sync tomorrow at 10am PT to review the numbers before we return to Sam?

Laura

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Sam Drake <sam@medtech.ai>, Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>

Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2027 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: MAP: Acme Health — cost stress test & evaluation checklist — initial answers + next steps

Sam / Acme team —

Thanks for the rapid follow-up. Quick answers and attachments included (see updated spreadsheet row highlights):

1) Variable prompt sizes: we re-ran the baseline with prompt=300 / gen=600. Baseline hosted cost increases from $0.0019 to $0.0032 per generated 1k tokens under the same kernel selection assumptions. Spreadsheet tab 'scenarios' row B shows the per-million token cost delta.

2) Caching: for your template header scenario (static 3–4 sentence header + variable patient json), prefix caching is a good win. Our modeled conservative hit rate (based on similar customers) is 20–30% token savings. The 'token-econ-sensitivity.xlsx' tab 'scenarios' shows a delta of ~22% cost reduction at 25% hit. We included a short note on what we consider cacheable (static instruction + system prompt; NOT variable patient payload).

3) Batching window used for the 2–3x throughput estimate was 15–25ms average batching window. In the spreadsheet we included three canonical windows (4ms, 8ms, 25ms) with p50/p95 numbers from the sandbox runs. Key takeaways: 4ms -> best latency, 25ms -> ~2.8x throughput with modest p95 increase for long requests.

4) Quantized model quality delta: Karthik added a small column with prior HelixMed summarization evals. Typical int8 quality drop observed was ~1.5–2.5% on rouge/semantic similarity; we recommend gating quantized rollout if the task requires >98% of float16 quality. See 'quality-delta' tab.

Gating language (from MAP, copied):
- Cost gate: proceed if observed per-month cost projection <= 25% above Redwood baseline OR Acme signs off on mitigation (larger batching / enable prefix caching).
- Latency gate: p95 must be <= 350ms for the full prompt size; else we will evaluate smaller context or different kernel.
- Quality gate: quantized variant allowed only if quality delta <= 3% on representative prompt set.

Next steps:
- Proposed 60-minute call: Wed 16 Jun, 10am PT to walk the scenario rows in the spreadsheet and confirm acceptance criteria.
- We will update the MAP PDF with the gating language and owners after the call and re-share.

Attachments: updated token-econ-sensitivity.xlsx (tabs: scenarios, quality-delta, rollout-gates), acme_map_v2.pdf (updated draft)

Best,
Laura Bennett
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
